attempts.summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) from scratch on RHEL9 (installed mariadb:10.11/galera module, configured wsrep, opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567/4568, verified SELinux port labels), bootstrapped node1 and joined node2/node3 via rsync SST, created an application database (appdb.customers) with sample rows, and confirmed multi-master writes replicate across all three. Added node4 as a fourth Galera member: installed the same stack, configured wsrep with the existing cluster's seed list, started it, and confirmed it received the full dataset via SST and both reads and writes work symmetrically across all four nodes (wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced). Then executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id and cluster health baselines, restarted each of the four nodes one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (never more than one down at once, preserving Galera quorum), polled until each came back, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified MariaDB auto-started, rejoined the cluster (size 4, Synced, wsrep_ready ON), and retained all data (7 rows) after each restart. Finished with a live cross-node write/read check (node1 write visible instantly on node4) proving the cluster is fully healthy post-restart.
